messages:
oliver: quick drop 14 — ran micro-decode chunking experiments on zephyr6b int4/int6 hybrid. major cost upside but some quality hits on long, citation-heavy prompts. posting numbers + a possible ops playbook.
maya: awesome, numbers pls + any sample failures?
oliver: short summary (slice=long-cited-articles, avg input ~1100 tokens, N=640):
```
- p95 latency: fp16 210ms | int6 240ms | int4 280ms
- tokens/sec: fp16 0.90 | int6 0.47 | int4 0.32
- cost/1k tokens: fp16 $0.0090 | int6 $0.0045 | int4 $0.0029
- recall@5 (gold): fp16 80.0% | int6 76.2% | int4 70.5%
- ROUGE-L drop: int6 ~2.8 pts | int4 ~6.1 pts
- hallucination proxy rate: fp16 2.0% | int6 4.8% | int4 9.4%
- note: chunked-decoding (first 384 tokens fp16, remainder int4) recovers most citation accuracy: recall@5 78.5%, rouge drop ~2.0 pts, cost ~ $0.0036/1k
```
link: https://internal.redwood/sparkbench/zephyr6b/3211112222
zarah: chunked decode looks promising  — cost close to int4 but quality near int6/fp16. what's infra complexity?
oliver: we can implement chunking as two back-to-back decode calls (runtime already supports streaming concatenation). small infra plumbing: tracer for continuity + KV cache glue for priming. microbench shows ~12% extra overhead but still huge econ win.
trent: ops/playbook ideas: mirror-probe for high-risk traffic, 1% canary with live chunked decode, and token-level fallback when hallucination proxy triggers. pseudocode below.
```
# routing + chunking + token-fallback
if request.tokens > 800 or citation_count >=2:
  route -> chunked(fp16_first=384, rest=int4)
else:
  route -> int4

# token-level fallback during decode
for each emitted_block:
  if hallucination_score(emitted_block) > 0.7:
    re-decode last_window in fp16 and replace output
    increment fallback_counter
```
maya: token-level fallback sounds powerful but could add latency spikes. what threshold & window would you suggest?
oliver: pragmatic defaults: hallucination_score threshold 0.7, check sliding window 64 tokens, allow up to 2 fallbacks per request, track 95th percentile fallback latency.
zarah: eval harness needs to capture: golden recall, rouge, hallucination proxy, user-flag rate, plus decode-fallback counts and latency. can we wire automatic golden-eval snapshots for mirrored probes?
trent: yes. plan: mirrored-probe (no user impact) for 72h where we store paired outputs (fp16 vs chunked-int4) and run golden eval nightly. parallel 2% canary where chunked-decoding is live for users. fallback -> immediate fp16 route for that session if persistent failures.
maya: for GTN/product decks i'll need monthly savings (three scenarios), exposure (traffic fraction & revenue-sensitive buckets), and fallback cost. oliver can you stub the numbers?
oliver: will do. quick econ notes: chunked decode ~= 2.5x token saving vs fp16 for large docs; if long-cited docs are 8% of traffic and represent 45% of retention-sensitive flows, net platform savings ~18-22% but risk concentrated.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: mirror-probe created: zephyr6b-chunk-mirror @100% long-cited requests (no user impact). canary job created: zephyr6b-chunk-canary @2% live. See https://internal.redwood/deploys/3211112222
zag: (reaction) :rocket:
maya: next steps: (1) run 72h mirror + nightly golden evals, (2) 2% canary live chunking with token-fallback enabled, (3) collect fallback latency + user-flag signals, (4) ryan (cc) to model churn sensitivity for slides. post interim metrics here.
oliver: i'll post 24h snapshot and a small sample of failure cases. tagging infra to help with KV glue. :white_check_mark:
